lines.text: DJ turn me up please. With eyes wide shut and my chin nested at the arc of the weight of these
spoken words, I have a story to tell. Of ghosts whispering unfolded delusions, birthed in purity
and dying and the veneers of sun-soaked evergreen fields are nourished. A love story of one by one
treasures escaping and devaluing themselves after defamed unsalted stars diminish their glares.
And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me
up. So I can speak of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a
shared home boxed in truck on separate one-way streets not built with u-turns or stop. Maybe
we shouldn't signs. A love story of years 11 years each plucked off as daisy pedals
we love we not. Of a future gone swiftly and a past left empty handed to pick a road of heavy rain
or a frontal fog or of dim night lights under a cloud with the silver lining. Of now turning
forth to face the lights and shadows one night at a time, one tear at a time. When called to a friend
at a time. One open mic at a time. Chin now nested high and volume turned up in a story to tell.

characters.name: POET
characters.who: THE POET, a man: a Black man in his thirties, dark brown skin, short faded haircut, full well-groomed beard, as in the reference photos. He is the speaker of every poem.

characters.name: EX
characters.who: THE EX, a man the poet loved. His FACE IS NEVER SEEN: paint him only from behind and three-quarter behind; the head is the back of the head (short dark hair, the nape, one ear at most). Broad shoulders, slightly taller than the poet.

passage.line: And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me
passage.why_fulcrum: The plea turns his love story into a claim to be heard. After it, the wedding bands and the boxed home read as testimony he crossed a divide to give, not as a lament.

answer.title: TULSA OKLAHOMA, ca. 1945 - ca. 1955
answer.said: so that all may be heard.
answer.why: He crossed the divide to be heard; the archive answers with the purpose itself, being heard by all. Same meaning, not just a shared word.

passage.gesture_detail: He holds the microphone out at arm's length toward the DJ booth, as if handing over his voice to be turned up, and keeps it there through the line.

plate.why: The DJ booth he is pleading to; the plate has a neon title over the booth, so a wall above the decks exists for the archive to open in.

passage.staging: POET at left facing the booth at right; the DJ at the decks; the archive opens in the wall under the neon title, above the DJ's head, between them.
